citation: Hammond and Cooperman (2022). Windfarm Operations and Maintenance cost-Benefit Analysis Tool (WOMBAT). National Renewable Energy Laboratory. https://doi.org/10.2172/1894867
description: WOMBAT is the national laboratory's discrete-event simulation of wind-farm operations and maintenance. It represents land-based or offshore turbine failures, repair tasks, crews, weather windows and operating costs. Inputs include a farm design, failure distributions, maintenance strategies, logistics and weather; outputs include time-based availability and annual operating-cost estimates. Farm size and simulation years follow the configuration, not a fixed site. Source is free under Apache-2.0, with PyPI installation, notebooks and documentation. The README warns that the package is still in development and that version 0.6 changes results under some conditions because of repair-model upgrades. Such model changes matter when comparing scenarios across releases. WOMBAT supports maintenance capacity and resilience planning for wind generation. It complements FOXES-style energy-yield calculations, but no coupled analysis was performed. The technical report describes comparisons with other models; those results were not reproduced here.
inputs: Wind farm assets, failures, maintenance and weather assumptions
name: WOMBAT wind-farm maintenance simulation
notes: G7 G7-1227. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
outputs: Availability, repair activity and annual operating costs
